title: Not every such grace converts: the ineffective desires
source_text: VI. Neque tamen eorum mens est, propriam hanc Christi gratiam hominem semper actu & reipsa convertere, & poenitentiam veram ac seriam in eo operari. Idque quoniam homo ea gratia motus, non semper vult aut agit efficaciter & perfecte quod volendum & agendum est: & saepe contingit hominem peccatorem in solis inefficacibus desideriis quae gratia efformavit haerere, nec ea ad operis effectum ob infirmitatem suam ac vitium proprium perducere; abjicere etiam desideria ista, & reluctante ac vincente concupiscentia, non resipiscere a peccato, non agere poenitentiam ut oportet, & quantum oportet ut a peccato resurgat, illiusque veniam a Deo consequatur.
pass_a_gloss: VI. Nor yet is it their mind, that this proper grace of Christ always converts a man in act and in reality, and works true and serious penitence in him. And that because man moved by that grace, does not always will or do efficaciously and perfectly what is to be willed and done: and often it happens that a sinful man sticks in the inefficacious desires alone which grace has formed, nor brings them through to the effect of the work because of his infirmity and his own fault; that he even throws away those desires, and with concupiscence resisting and conquering, does not recover from sin, does not do penitence as he ought, and as much as he ought that he may rise again from sin, and obtain pardon of it from God.
pass_b_english: Thesis VI. They do not, however, claim that this grace proper to Christ always actually converts a person and produces true and earnest repentance in him. For someone moved by it does not always will or do, effectively and fully, what ought to be willed and done.

A sinner often gets stuck in the merely ineffective desires that grace has shaped in him, and through his own weakness and fault does not carry them through to the deed. He may even cast those desires aside, and as concupiscence fights back and wins, fail to turn from sin, or to repent as he should and as much as he must to rise from sin and receive God's forgiveness.

choices.why: Poenitentia covers both inner repentance and its works; 'repentance' in the reading, 'penitence' in the literal pass.

bible_refs: Cornelius Jansenius, Augustinus (Louvain, 1640), tome 3, De gratia Christi Salvatoris.
